evidence.claim: Aura cloud management API authenticates via OAuth 2.0 with self-serve account-linked credentials
evidence.quote: The Aura API uses OAuth 2.0 for API authentication. API credentials are linked to the user account, inheriting its capabilities and roles.

evidence.claim: Public REST-style HTTP and Query APIs are documented alongside many client drivers and a GraphQL library
Neo4j officially ships and documents an MCP server on its own docs site
evidence.quote: Neo4j MCP implements the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard that lets applications connect to external data sources and tools.

notes: Legacy REST API (rest-docs v3.5) is deprecated and removed in Neo4j 4.0: 'The API described in this manual been deprecated and will be removed in Neo4j 4.0.' Use the Query API / HTTP API or Bolt drivers instead. Official MCP server is downloadable as a binary and works with Aura and self-hosted deployments. Token-based (bearer) auth with the Query API is documented via community/OIDC guides. Pricing page shows paid Aura tiers, but local self-hosted usage (localhost:7474 examples) and account-linked Aura credentials are self-serve.
